name: Yarrow
grown_as: A native perennial wild flower of grassland and lawns, also grown in gardens; garden varieties come in pinks, reds and yellows. Drawn as the wild white form. ⚠️ CHECK if William grows a coloured variety.
habit: A spreading patch from creeping roots, with low feathery leaves and upright, tough, woolly flowering stems 20 to 60 cm, unbranched until the flower heads

leaf.arrangement: Basal tuft; alternate up the stem
leaf.type: Compound, two or three times pinnately divided into very many narrow segments
leaf.outline: Long and narrow, strap- to lance-shaped, 5 to 15 cm long and 1 to 3 cm wide, feathery and three-dimensional
leaf.base: Narrowing to a short stalk; stem leaves stalkless, clasping
leaf.margin: Every segment ends in a fine point; no teeth as such
leaf.surface: Soft, with scattered woolly hairs; aromatic when crushed
leaf.stalk: Short on basal leaves, none on stem leaves

flower.form: Many tiny daisy flower heads packed into a flat-topped cluster
flower.petals: Each head has about five broad ray florets (the petals), each with three small teeth at the tip
flower.centre: A small disc of cream to yellowish florets, turning grey-brown
flower.behind: Overlapping green bracts with brown papery edges under each head
flower.carried: In dense flat-topped or slightly domed clusters at the top of the stems
flower.size: Each head 4 to 6 mm; the cluster 5 to 10 cm across

fruit: Tiny flat grey-brown seeds with no pappus, in heads that dry to brown flat clusters
seedling: Two small oval seed leaves, then first true leaves narrow and toothed, soon feathery
winter: Green feathery leaves stay through winter; dead brown flower stems with flat seed heads stand

leaf: long narrow feathery leaf, finely divided two or three times
many tiny segments on both sides of the midrib
bloom: flat-topped cluster of many tiny heads
each head with about five broad white rays
seed: tiny flat grey-brown seed with no parachute
seedling: first true leaf narrow, toothed or feathery
young: low tuft of long narrow feathery leaves
flower: upright stems topped with flat white clusters
seedhead: flat brown dried clusters on stiff stems
dormant: dead brown stems with flat heads

look_alikes: Sneezewort (Achillea ptarmica) has undivided toothed leaves and fewer, larger heads. Umbellifers like cow parsley have broader leaflets and umbels of tiny five-petalled flowers, not daisy heads. Mayweeds have single larger daisy heads.
